Primordial Light (Korean: 최초의 빛, chwechoe bit, "First Light") is Moonlight Cookie's fourth Costume, released in the first half of the Labyrinth of Remembrance update.

It is a Legendary Costume that can be obtained either by drawing it from the Costume Gacha or by purchasing it in the Rainbow Crystal Shop. Obtaining Primordial Light also unlocks the Lobby Design The Hall of Time and Light, as well as a Costume for Dreamcatcher,  Night Sky Suncatcher.

Story

A very long time ago, there was the first Cookie made by the hands of the wizards. Baked through the most intricate and sweet magic, this Cookie was so beautiful it sparkled with light. Proud of their work, the wizards gave this Cookie the name Primordial Light.

Trivia

  • Primordial Light was released alongside  Glass Atrium Respite,  Night Sky Suncatcher, and  Gentleman Bee.
  • Primordial Light's hat features a very small star on it, which resembles the Little Star used to upgrade Moonlight Cookie's Magic Candy.
  • It is speculated that Primordial Light is either Moonlight Cookie herself, or a completely different Cookie altogether. This comes from a wide range of seemingly conflicting evidence, as the description for the Costume states that the Cookie that the wizards created was called "Primordial Light" rather than "Moonlight Cookie," it is also addressed as "it" rather than "she" (though this may be a simple semantics or translation issue), and the Korean version of the game directly calls the Costume "First Light Cookie.", there is also the fact that Primordial Light was originally supposed to be an entire separate Cookie, named Sugar Cube Cookie.
    • However, in the Labyrinth of Remembrance story, Primordial Light can be seen on a stained glass window, and GingerBright mentions that the smile seen in the stained glass is "like moonlight." This may imply Primordial Light is indeed related to, or otherwise is, Moonlight Cookie. though it could be possible that the story was not actually referring to Primordial Light when focused on the image of it, though, as Primordial Light's stained glass has no smile while the regular Moonlight Cookie stained glass does, and the staff is said to resemble Paradise Compass, which it only does in Moonlight Cookie's default appearance.
  • Primordial Light is said to be the first creation of the wizards.
  • Primordial Light's gacha illustration seems to feature a modified edit of one of its sprites.
  • Primordial Light and  Milky Way are the only Costumes for Moonlight Cookie to have a bonus effect for Star Powder Jellies.
  • Primordial Light's staff can be seen in the background alongside Moonlight Cookie's other Costumes' in Sugar Glass Cookie's Trial.

Alluring Crescent Moon (Korean: 매혹의 그믐달, maehoge geumeumttal, "Enchanting Dark Moon") is Moonlight Cookie's third Costume, released during the Merry Winter Parade! update. It is a Super Epic Costume that can be obtained either by drawing it from the Costume Gacha or by purchasing it in the Rainbow Crystal Shop.

Story

On the darkest of nights, the red moon lights a scarlet path. Unbeknownst to most, following the path leads to a trap of eternal nightmares.

Trivia

  • Alluring Crescent Moon was released alongside  Blissful Full Moon.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon is based around the crescent moon lunar phase and also a variation of the lunar eclipse, blood moons.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon, as opposed to Moonlight Cookie's other Costumes, appears to have a more angular design, with lots of sharp ends. This can be seen especially with Costume's hair, as it is straighter and more sharp in contrast to Moonlight Cookie's soft and wavy hair.
    • Additionally, Alluring Crescent Moon's staff also adds a scythe-like design, possibly to emphasize on the crescent element featured in the Costume.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon, like  Blissful Full Moon, was only available as either an Event Reward or purchasable by its Package. This has changed upon the introduction of the Costume Gacha and has since been made permanent.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon is referred to as "darkMoon" in the files.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon's staff can be seen in the background alongside Moonlight Cookie's other Costumes' in Sugar Glass Cookie's Trial.
  • Alluring Crescent Moon appears in Cookie Run: Kingdom as a corrupted version of Moonlight Cookie from a timeline conquered by Shadow Milk Cookie.

Changelog

  • Labyrinth of Remembrance - October 26, 2021
    • Reduced Twinkling Star Jelly points.

Blissful Full Moon (Korean: 환희의 보름달, hwanhie boreumttal, "Jubilant Full Moon") is Moonlight Cookie's second Costume, released during the Merry Winter Parade! update. It is a Super Epic Costume that can be obtained either by drawing it from the Costume Gacha or by purchasing it in the Rainbow Crystal Shop.

Story

The full moon bathes the world with brilliant radiance. All who gaze upon this spectacle find it impossible to sleep.

Trivia

  • Blissful Full Moon was released alongside  Alluring Crescent Moon.
  • Even though Blissful Full Moon is a Super Epic Costume, it does not have a different set of liked and disliked gifts nor does it have a different set of lobby quotes like other Super Epic Costumes.
    •  Alluring Crescent Moon, however, does have a different set of liked and disliked gifts and a different set of lobby quotes: thus making the case with Blissful Full Moon stranger.
    • It is also similar to  Milky Way, which doesn't have any unique quotes at all.
  • Blissful Full Moon's staff can be seen in the background alongside Moonlight Cookie's other Costumes' in Sugar Glass Cookie's Trial.
  • Blissful Full Moon, like  Alluring Crescent Moon, was only available as either an Event Reward or purchasable by its Package. This has changed upon the introduction of the Costume Gacha and has since been made permanent.
  • Blissful Full Moon had an oversight where its Bonus Time sprite seems to be placed awkwardly in regard to the Cookie's hitbox, resulting in a dissonance between where the hitbox should be, and the sprite itself.
    • This was later fixed in The Sweet Signals From Space update, almost four years after the Costume's release. Though, this fix resulted in the removal of the veil that surrounded the Costume's Skill and Bonus Time sprites.
  • Blissful Full Moon was ranked first place in the 2019 Costume of the Year, making it the Costume's highest ranking yet. It then ranked again as one of the top 24 Costumes in the 2021 Costume of the Year.

Changelog

  • The Sweet Signals From Space - December 28, 2023
    • Fixed the Bonus Time image for the Costume.
  • Labyrinth of Remembrance - October 26, 2021
    • Reduced Twinkling Star Jelly points.

Milky Way (Korean: 밀키웨이, milkiwaei) is Moonlight Cookie's first Costume, released during the Dr. Wasabi Cookie and Mustard Cookie! update. It is a Super Epic Costume that can be obtained by drawing it from the Vintage Costume Jar in the Gem Exchange Center.

Story

Countless stars twinkle in the twilight of an endless dream. Close your eyes, and you'll hear a lovely lullaby.

Trivia

  • Milky Way was the first Costume to be made for a Legendary Cookie.
  • Milky Way is the only Super Epic Costume that does not provide its owner with any new quotes, likely due to its age.
  • Milky Way,  Guardian of the Millennial Tree, and  Lord of Ash are the only Super Epic Costumes in the game to not have their own illustration. This could be due to the fact they are not in the Costume Gacha.
  • Previously, this Costume was only obtained by purchasing it with 4,000 League Medals in the Medal Exchange Center, until it was rehauled for the rework of Champions League, the Costume was then moved to the Land's End Shop instead. Currently, it can be pulled from the Vintage Costume Jar in the Gem Exchange Center
  • Milky Way was one of only two non-limited Costumes that could've been obtained from the Land's End Shop, the other being  Guardian of the Millennial Tree.
  • Milky Way's staff can be seen in the background alongside Moonlight Cookie's other Costumes' in Sugar Glass Cookie's Trial.
  • Milky Way was ranked as one of the top 24 Costumes in the 2021 Costume of the Year.
  • Milky Way's name likely derives from the name of our own galaxy, the Milky Way.
